speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin carried water up from the river in your best basket. The basket has kept almost everything except the water, which is now on your cousin.
left result: A clay lining. It holds a mouthful of water, then slumps.
left effects: unmark drips; look lined-basket; set lined; next tut-2
right result: A pot-shaped lump. It holds water briefly, then rejoins the ground.
right effects: unmark drips; look clay-pot; next tut-2
notes: Scene 1 of the outline: introduce the object and two approaches

speaker: cousin
text: The sides collapse when lifted. Your cousin suggests never lifting it. That is a real option, and you are not taking it.
left result: It stands up on its own. It also takes two people to carry.
left effects: observe holds-shape; look thick-pot; next tut-3
right result: A rolled rim stiffens the whole thing. It holds its shape.
right effects: observe holds-shape; look rim-pot; next tut-3

speaker: naysayer
text: It dried hard in the sun. Then it rained, and the dried vessel became mud again. The Naysayer says this is what mud is for.
left result: A day and a night beside the fire. Then a small, sad ping.
left effects: danger +1; observe survives-heat; look cracked-pot; mark smoke; next tut-4; death vessel-kiln
right result: The fire roars. So does your cousin, who was standing too close.
right effects: danger +2; observe survives-heat; look cracked-pot; mark flames; next tut-4; death vessel-kiln
notes: Scene 3: introduce Danger and useful failure

speaker: cousin
text: The first test cracked. The smaller piece survived, and it rings when you tap it. Your cousin has tapped it forty times.
left result: Slow in, slow out. It comes out whole, and it holds water.
left effects: unmark smoke; unmark flames; observe holds-water; look fired-pot if not lined; look woven-pot if lined
right result: A ring of stones, a roof of turf. It comes out ringing.
right effects: danger +1; unmark smoke; unmark flames; observe holds-water; look fired-pot if not lined; look woven-pot if lined; death vessel-kiln
notes: Scene 4: the final observation. A lined basket burns away and leaves its weave

speaker: cousin
text: It holds water. It holds water all night, without complaint. People have started bringing requests, and your cousin is keeping a list on a flat rock.
left result: Small pots, one per family, each slightly wrong in its own way.
left effects: commit pottery; legacy pottery-household; look household-pots
right result: One enormous jar. The whole village's food fits inside.
right effects: commit pottery; legacy pottery-communal; look store-jar
notes: Scene 5: commit pottery and seed the legacy

speaker: cousin
text: The vessel is ready for its big test, in front of everyone. Nobody has checked whether it's ready.
left result: It drinks the river, slowly and with dignity.
right result: It drinks the soup, then the table.
notes: Unreachable in the tutorial (every branch reaches pottery); here so a changed tutorial can never strand a life

speaker: neighbours
text: Everyone wants one immediately. The neighbours want two, and they would like to know how you did it, very casually.
left result: Soon everyone makes pots. Some of them are even pots.
right result: Pots stay rare, well made and yours. The neighbours stop being casual.
right effects: set guarded; danger +1; next tut-7; death vessel-kiln

speaker: mother
text: Your mother has filled a vessel with damp grain and pressed the lid down tight. It has begun to smell like a decision.
left result: A tighter lid. The smell stays inside, for now, like a promise.
left effects: unmark damp-grain; set lid-habit; next tut-8
right: Tell her to dry it first.
right result: She dries it on the roof. The birds are delighted. The grain keeps.
right effects: unmark damp-grain; set drying-habit; next tut-8
notes: Scene 7: the next practical problem Shows the mother's own lidded pot; tut-8 puts the legacy look back.

speaker: elder
shows: look household-pots if legacy pottery-household; look store-jar if legacy pottery-communal
text: Your workshop has become an institution. It has a queue, a rival across the river and a name you didn't choose. They want your final advice.
left result: They carve it over the workshop door. Nobody can read yet, but they like it.
right result: The elder volunteers so quickly he was clearly waiting.
notes: Scene 8: finalize the legacy and close the life
